title: Ensure a single Follow Stream is running only
description:
When changing one of the selection parameters in the Follow Stream
dialog while a filtering task is already running, the result is
inaccurate.
While a filtering task is already running in the Follow Stream
dialog, any filter change which triggers a new filtering gives a
wrong result. Both the displayed data and the Save As functions
are impacted. Closes #15637

Why go into the loop in the first place, if you are going to break hard anyway? I would if-clause the loop and jump over it, if the read is happening.

Or better yet, https://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qmutex.html use a Mutex. Makes much more sense in this case, and avoids changing quite a few things

Will we break the loop or not, it depends on the time needed for displaying all the data (it can be so fast that there is no opportunity for breaking) and on the user changing either the direction or the encoding while it's still running. Please note that when this dialog is first opened, these two are disabled and we must wait, which is not completely consistent with what I am adding.

I will give a chance to the Mutex quickly as suggested.

I absolutely get that, I just hate adding a simple variable to the header, just for a single use-case. Even static inside the method would be better in my opinion, but it needs resetting, which is why the current method was surely chosen.

But you break with the very first instruction inside the loop. You have to keep in mind, the g_list lookup functions are expensive. So even if you call this code a bunch of times, and break every time except the first, the lookup functions are being run. It would make much more sense to break not inside the loop, but make it a condition for the loop itself or guard the loop with an if-clause checking for the readinprogress.

Using the _readinprogress_ at `readFollowStream()` level to decide if we should enter the loop or not isn't working well because one can still make another choice for the direction or the encoding (which update _follow_info/show_type_). The result : less packets than expected which is the opposite problem of the bug filled.
We could move the _readinprogress_ at the _on_cbXXX_ functions but the user would feel like changing the selection doesn't do anything. In this case, isn't it better to rather disable the selections when a job is running like it is done during the first execution ?

Let's take a bad scenario when we also force the user to wait : each job taking t time, and the user changes both the direction and the encoding, the total waiting time is 3*t (minimum, hexdump being much slower for example). Without the interruption possibility, that might be a bad user experience.

Thanks for the remarks on the header variable, I'll make something more compliant to the expected quality. But please clarify which direction I should go.

For me, this is a simple helper variable. As said, better would be a Mutex as it is actually what this would be. I just want to avoid, that we bloat the header files with informations, that are not actually needed someplace else.

But I would be ok leaving it be.
